expected_evidence: Ice-core geochemical anomalies in Greenland cores (GISP2, GRIP, NGRIP) at the ~12,900 cal BP (younger-dryas onset) horizon: spikes in cosmogenic isotopes (10Be, 36Cl) consistent with enhanced atmospheric ionization from a gamma-ray/cosmic-ray flux event

Platinum, iridium, and nanodiamond/magnetic-spherule concentrations in the Younger Dryas boundary layer (widely reported at other sites, would be expected co-located in Greenland ice or adjacent sediment cores)
Anomalous 14C production spike in tree-ring/varve records synchronous with the proposed gamma-ray ionization event
Black mat / soot and biomass-burning markers in terrestrial sediment sequences near 12,900 BP indicating continent-scale wildfires triggered by atmospheric ionization or Taurid-complex fragmentation
Astronomical/meteoritic records: dust layer or extraterrestrial-flux markers (He-3, Ir) tied to Taurid stream encounter in the same ice strata
Genetic bottleneck signatures in North American megafauna and Clovis-era human populations dated to the interval
Model-prior literature on the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis and Taurid-complex encounter models (unverified, low-tier)
response.rationale: The interval [-12000,-11001] BCE aligns with the Younger Dryas onset (~12,900 cal BP), so the 'younger-dryas' detectability row is the appropriate baseline rather than 'upper-paleolithic'. The hypothesis's placement (Greenland ice sheet) is fortunate for detectability: polar ice cores are exceptionally well-preserved, continuously and highly resolved archives that have been intensively studied for exactly this time window (GISP2/GRIP/NGRIP), giving geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7) evidence kinds strong survival and detection odds — any large cosmogenic-isotope or extraterrestrial-flux spike at this horizon would very likely already have been picked up by existing high-resolution sampling. Material (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence (megafaunal extinction, Clovis disruption, biomass-burning layers) are more degraded/ambiguous over 13,000 years, consistent with the ongoing controversy over the broader Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis. The specific mechanism 'gamma-ray ionization' is not a standard, well-established trigger in the literature I'm aware of — the mainstream hypothesis invokes cometary/bolide airburst or Taurid-stream fragment impacts producing platinum/iridium/nanodiamond signatures, while a distinct 'gamma-ray-ionization' pathway (e.g., a nearby transient high-energy event enhancing atmospheric ionization/cloud nucleation) is a more speculative variant; I flag this as model-prior and unverified. Given the high preservation and research intensity of Greenland ice records for this exact interval, the absence of unambiguous evidence in the literature for a gamma-ray-ionization signature is somewhat informative against the hypothesis rather than purely a detectability failure — hence a moderate-to-fair aggregate detectability adjustment (~0.55) rather than a low one, weighting the strong ice-core/geological/astronomical channels against weaker material/genetic channels.
